source.author: verg
source.text: Hinc Troïus omnis Tyrrhenusque ruit variis exercitus armis, haud secus instructi ferro, quam si aspera Martis pugna vocet; nec non mediis in milibus ipsi ductores auro volitant ostroque decori, et genus Assaraci Mnestheus et fortis Asilas et Messapus equum domitor, Neptunia proles.
source.text_original: Hinc Troïus omnis / Tyrrhenusque ruit variis exercitus armis, / haud secus instructi ferro, quam si aspera Martis / pugna vocet; nec non mediis in milibus ipsi / ductores auro volitant ostroque decori, / et genus Assaraci Mnestheus et fortis Asilas / et Messapus equum domitor, Neptunia proles.
source.text_english: From here the whole Trojan and Tyrrhenian host rushes on, armed with varied weapons, just as well arrayed in steel as if the rough battle of Mars were calling them; and in the midst of the thousands the leaders themselves also fly forth, adorned with gold and purple: Mnestheus, of the line of Assaracus, and brave Asilas, and Messapus, tamer of horses, descendant of Neptune.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: securus in aequor haut minus Erginus, proles Neptunia, fertur, qui maris insidias, clarae qui sidera noctis norit et e clausis quem destinet Aeolus antris, non metuat cui regna ratis, cui tradere caelum assidua Tiphys vultum lassatus ab Arcto.
reuse.text_original: securus in aequor / haut minus Erginus, proles Neptunia, fertur, / qui maris insidias, clarae qui sidera noctis / norit et e clausis quem destinet Aeolus antris, / non metuat cui regna ratis, cui tradere caelum / assidua Tiphys vultum lassatus ab Arcto.
reuse.text_english: Secure, into the sea is borne Erginus, no less so, a child of Neptune, one who knows the sea’s ambushes, one who knows the stars of the clear night and whom Aeolus dispatches from his closed caves, who need not fear the ship’s dominion, to whom Tiphys, worn out by constant watch, wishes to entrust the sky, steering from the North.
